newsitem.title: USA: Orlando airport cargo buildings open.
newsitem.headline: Orlando airport cargo buildings open.

text.p: Orlando International Airport's first two new cargo buildings have opened and the first two tenants have moved in, an airport executive told Reuters Wednesday.
"The developer has had a lot of inquiries," Ken St. Amand, Orlando Airport's cargo marketing manager, said.
Walt Disney Co affiliate Walt Disney Attractions and Action International, a freight forwarder and customs broker have moved into the first two buildings of the new cargo facility.
The complex, built on 19.16 acres, is being developed by Mantovani Investments Inc, Orlando. Seven buildings are planned with more than 200,000 square feet of space.
The first building has 37,840 square feet and the second 11,352 square feet, according to the Greater Orlando Aviation Authority.
Disney uses the free trade zone facility to store -- and import as needed -- items for its Epcot Center international theme park, St. Amand said.
